chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zureyq ibn al-Zubayr, from Sadeyr, that he heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying:

Whoever says, when he applies the lime paste (for hair removal): 'O Allah, make good what is clean from me, and purify what is good from me, and replace for me with clean hair that does not disobey You. O Allah, I have purified myself seeking the Sunnah of the Messengers, and seeking Your pleasure and Your forgiveness, so prohibit my hair and my skin from the Fire, and purify my creation, and make good my character, and purify my deeds, and make me from those who meet You upon the upright, tolerant religion of Ibrahim, Your friend, and the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), Your beloved and Your Messenger, acting by Your laws, following the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), holding fast to it, being well-educated by the excellence of Your education, and the education of Your Messenger, and the education of Your Guardians, whom You nourished with Your education, and planted wisdom in their chests, and made them mines for Your knowledge, may Your blessings be upon them.'

Whoever says that, Allah will purify him from the filth in the world and from the sins, and replace for him with hair that does not disobey Allah, and Allah will create for every hair from his body an angel who glorifies Him for him until the Hour is established, and indeed one glorification from their glorifications equals one thousand glorifications from the glorification of the people of the earth.

key_terms.النُّورَة: A lime paste used for hair removal

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for hair removal (Al-Noura) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this supplication links physical grooming to spiritual refinement, reflecting the concept of *fitrah* (natural purity) where bodily cleanliness serves as a vessel for moral and ritual purity. The promise of an angel for each hair underscores the cosmic significance of minor acts of worship, while the invocation for 'Hanifiyyah' connects the individual to the pristine monotheism of Ibrahim and the Sunnah of the Prophet. This practice is often viewed not merely as hygiene but as a means of preparing the body for prayer and divine encounter.
